summary.prose: Build the installed macOS supervisor and route existing shell, TUI, and daemon lifecycle paths through it. Add rollback-compatible update validation, durable recovery, and correlated completion in VS Code and JetBrains. Run targeted tests per task, then qualify the installed route and run the full sweep.

tasks.title: Define the managed lifecycle wire contract
tasks.summary: Implement bounded frame parsing, stable hello negotiation, typed requests and receipts, operation-specific field validation, and the controller and inherited channel roles.
acceptanceChecks: A mismatched release or version cannot issue a lifecycle command
Lease, update and drain fields are accepted only for the documented operations

tests.name: Wrong peer, root and generation
Protocol version, frame bounds, channel role and request correlation
Discriminated ownership-conflict, exit-unconfirmed, supervisor-unavailable and watchdog errors
Lease token, channel and generation mismatch
Update lock, version refusal and terminal outcome
Missing, misplaced, reused and stale lease tokens
Hello negotiates the highest common version and rejects peer identity mismatch, malformed hello and empty overlap

tasks.title: Add Darwin job and peer identity primitives
tasks.summary: Implement the narrow Darwin support for Unix peer PID and UID, process incarnation, read-only exit observation and verified per-user launch-job ownership. Package the platform-specific entry points and keep the Linux process broker unchanged.
acceptanceChecks: Peer mismatch, reused PID, wrong launch domain and unverified job removal fail closed
Darwin observations work without a Mach task right and Linux packaging remains intact

Idle stop, launch-domain refusal, missing runtime, reserved watchdog capacity and confirmed failed-exit classification
Hello negotiates the highest common version and rejects peer identity mismatch, malformed hello and empty overlap
Admission rejects foreign update IDs, owner PID reuse and connections opened before lease publication
Recovery job and legacy migration
Managed Darwin never invokes the Mach broker from either the controller or shutdown watchdog
Legacy exit observation rejects PID reuse, owner mismatch and timeout without invoking the Mach broker
Distinct test roots reject cross-root control and label collisions
Legacy socket peer UID or PID differs from the registered process incarnation

tasks.title: Implement the installation mutation gate and journal
tasks.summary: Add installation-local arbitration, durable controller identity and reservations, transaction stages and recovery decisions. Serialize ordinary restart as a single reservation. Bind each mutation to the current owner and update ID where applicable.
acceptanceChecks: Stale sockets, reused owner PID, unrelated controllers and orphan reservations cannot mutate
Recovery branches on the matching durable outcome before any destructive action

Admission rejects foreign update IDs, owner PID reuse and connections opened before lease publication
Crash recovery classifies the durable outcome before deciding rollback or activation
Supervisor loss, concurrent restart and stale files
Race competing start, stop, raw shutdown and update against both supervisor versions
Kill the controller at reservation, job registration, probation, and after outcome publication
Public RPC arm gets busy during update while an admitted drain and local signal preserve their watchdog path

tasks.title: Implement the supervisor child lifecycle
tasks.summary: Build the per-user parent state machine, pinned child spawn, inherited channel, start/stop deadlines, exact escalation and reap, confirmed receipts and predecessor-bound replay. Start the supervisor idle and require journaled predecessor evidence during replacement.
acceptanceChecks: A hung or partially initialized child cannot be replaced before exact reap
An old stop or readiness frame cannot act on a newer generation

Discriminated ownership-conflict, exit-unconfirmed, supervisor-unavailable and watchdog errors

Hung before shutdown reply and hung native close after watchdog readiness
Supervisor loss, concurrent restart and stale files

Fresh supervisor first start requires durable predecessor evidence and an admitted owner

tasks.title: Delegate the run-file guard for managed children
tasks.summary: Have the supervisor own the existing guard and issue generation-scoped grants for child startup and listener close. Capture partial publication and reconcile only identity-proven files before releasing the guard.
acceptanceChecks: Forced close and partial startup release the supervisor-owned guard only after verified reap and reconciliation
Foreign or orphan guard and legacy Linux behavior remain fail-closed

Hold a client connection open during managed server.close and confirm forced reap releases the supervisor guard and permits exactly one restart
Kill startup child before PID, after PID, and after socket publication before ready
Kill the supervisor while it owns the guard and verify fail-closed operator recovery

tasks.title: Wire managed daemon readiness, shutdown and watchdog
tasks.summary: Integrate inherited ready/drain/arm and public shutdown admission in the daemon and both dispatch modes. Preserve local-signal emergency behavior and legacy/Linux broker routes. Avoid enabling installed rollout until the controller and updater are wired.
acceptanceChecks: Public shutdown cannot bypass an update reservation
Admitted drains and local signals keep independent generation-bound deadlines, with no managed Mach broker call

tasks.title: Route installed shell and TUI lifecycle through the supervisor
tasks.summary: Use one predecessor-bound restart in both entry points, stage the per-user launch job and require verified quiescence for legacy cutover. Add status and operator recovery access independent of a live daemon. Keep installed activation gated on end-to-end rollout readiness.
acceptanceChecks: Start, stop and restart share the installation gate and do not issue a second stop
CLI status shows recovery state when the daemon socket is unavailable

tasks.title: Enforce rollback-compatible startup and probation
tasks.summary: Define the release compatibility declarations and read-only quiesced checks. Validate before live boot effects. Gate graph migrations, cleanup, indexing and normal IPC until the candidate observes matching durable success.
acceptanceChecks: A newer graph schema or an unqualified release is refused before candidate writes
Candidate readiness verifies store opens and paused indexer initialization with no production indexing

tests.name: Compatibility declaration and read-only quiesced check refuse unknown or migration-bearing pairs
Hold application RPCs and indexing until matching durable success across threaded and non-threaded status paths
Inject upgrade with a newer graph schema and verify the old daemon can still open the unchanged store

tasks.title: Stage releases and hand off the launch job
tasks.summary: Pin releases, stage the detached helper behind the acknowledgement handoff and journal job admission separately from child launch. Verify old job exit and new handshake, then start and validate the candidate in probation. Return exact stage receipts for commit and rollback.
acceptanceChecks: The helper cannot mutate before acknowledgement handoff
An ambiguous launch registration or failed hello produces a bounded, identity-scoped handoff receipt
Candidate admission records exact predecessor evidence and keeps the release selector provisional

tests.name: Rollback after legacy stop but before managed readiness restores the saved service
Daemon-initiated update survives supervisor unload and writes one terminal result across a protocol version change
Fail hello after candidate job registration before child start, remove the candidate job and restore the prior release
Race competing start, stop, raw shutdown and update against both supervisor versions
Kill the controller at reservation, job registration, probation, and after outcome publication
Relaunch supervisor after provisional release selection and verify recovery restores the old selector before uncommitted rollback, or preserves the candidate after success
Fresh supervisor first start requires durable predecessor evidence and an admitted owner
Lost update acknowledgement neither permits an unacknowledged helper to mutate before response write nor triggers duplicate admission

tasks.title: Commit or recover the managed update transaction
tasks.summary: Use the journal to commit, roll back or retain a recovery fence. Verify candidate job removal and predecessor restoration, atomically write one outcome, and allow post-commit recovery to finish activation without rollback.
acceptanceChecks: Failed hello after registration removes only the verified candidate job before restoring the prior release
Controller loss before commit rolls back only with verified ownership; loss after commit preserves the selected release
Unresolved ownership remains fenced and a terminal outcome appears only after the verified decision

tasks.title: Project managed update state through daemon IPC
tasks.summary: Publish optional update IDs in managed acknowledgements and outcomes. Use a shared request-time installed-commit projection for threaded and non-threaded status. Preserve the existing fields and unmanaged behavior.
acceptanceChecks: The candidate commit remains hidden from old clients until durable success
A matching terminal outcome and status report the committed or restored release consistently

Candidate status projects the prior commit during validation and a later rollback in both IDE confirmation flows
Hold application RPCs and indexing until matching durable success across threaded and non-threaded status paths

tasks.title: Correlate update confirmation in VS Code and JetBrains
tasks.summary: Both IDEs confirm managed transactions only on their acknowledged update ID and show pending confirmation when the outcome cannot be retrieved. Keep the existing fallback for legacy responses.
acceptanceChecks: Changed installedCommit and unrelated terminal results do not confirm a managed update
Both IDEs handle rollback, lost acknowledgement and a legacy daemon

tests.name: Correlated update outcomes ignore unrelated terminal records and changed installedCommit
Candidate status projects the prior commit during validation and a later rollback in both IDE confirmation flows
Lost update acknowledgement neither permits an unacknowledged helper to mutate before response write nor triggers duplicate admission

tasks.title: Qualify installed rollout and run the final sweep
tasks.summary: Exercise the installed macOS LaunchAgent on disposable roots and regular Apple Silicon, including hung close, partial boot, legacy cutover, version-changing rollback and recovery. Verify Linux regressions, then run the complete sweep after all implementation tasks.
acceptanceChecks: Installed smoke proves verified generation change and safe rollback
All implementation tasks have relevant targeted test evidence before the final sweep
Managed installed activation is release-qualified only after the installed smoke and regression checks pass
